messages:
Anya K: quick check — I ran a small bring-up for the new 14B-int8 quant build (batching=auto, kv-cache on) against our product prompt suite. latency p95 sits at 120ms (within SLO), token cost down ~2.8x vs fp16. quality: micro-evals stable on avg, but we saw a small regress on the finance Q&A set — some hallucinations on ticker mapping (~1.7% of samples).

Mike R: can you paste the unit economics? numbers + assumptions please.

Anya K: sure. assumptions: baseline fp16 @ $0.010/token, int8 @ $0.0036/token (model + infra normalized), avg response length 80 tokens. so per-request cost: fp16 =~ $0.80, int8 =~ $0.29. throughput observed: int8 peak tokens/s +45% vs fp16 on same infra.

Lina G: that cost delta is great. product will worry about hallucination risk — what's the breakdown by severity? is it low-confidence answers or confidently wrong?

Anya K: mostly confident but wrong on entity linking (ticker & organization aliasing). examples: answered "ACME" -> wrong ticker. rate higher on prompts with short context. I pushed a quick eval summary here: https://redwood-console/internal/evals/1799043210 (note: internal link).

Eva: could this be quantization noise vs dataset bias? how does int4 look?

Anya K: int4 experiments look worse on the same subset — hallucinations up ~4.5%. int8 seems to be the practical sweet spot for now. int4 could be OK for embeddings-only or constrained generation, but not general Q&A.

Sam H: from a rollout perspective we should consider routing: default to int8 for free-tier/low-risk flows, fallback to fp16 for finance/legal critical paths. Also add a quality gate for canary.

Mike R: +1. Proposal: create a canary route for 5% traffic on int8 with an eval harness that monitors real-time regression on the finance prompt set. threshold: auto-rollback if >2% absolute drop in accuracy or >1.5% increase in high-confidence hallucinations over baseline.

Anya K: I can wire up the canary. eval command I used locally: ```bash
python eval_harness.py --model redwood/14b-int8 --prompts datasets/finance_short.json --out ./results/14b-int8-canary.json --metrics rouge,factuality,conf_rate
```

deploy-bot: deploy request created: canary/14b-int8 -> infra-cluster-3 (5% traffic). PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/982

Lina G: product question — will latency budget hold with the extra fallback routing? we can't add >30ms tail for finance flow.

Sam H: fallback only triggers on explicit mismatch or timeout failures. route decision is local (edge sidecar) so additional hop ~= 6-10ms. still within budget. we should set per-request timeout 800ms for canary so we avoid long tails.

Eva: plan sounds good. action items: 1) Anya -> wire canary + continuous eval (EOD) 2) Sam -> implement routing rule + timeout 3) Mike -> write rollback thresholds into runbook 4) Lina -> confirm product accepts 5% canary on Thurs.

Mike R: I'll draft the runbook short snippet for ops: "canary-int8: monitor accuracy_finance, high_conf_halluc_rate, latency_p95. rollback if any threshold breached for 15m window."

Anya K: one more note — recommend adding a small synthetic prefix-caching layer for finance prompts (many repeats). that reduces tokens and reduces the hallucination surface by keeping more context in the KV cache. cheap win.

Lina G: love that. thanks team. :thumbsup:

Mike R: let's re-eval after 48h of canary traffic and then decide on staged increase (5% -> 20% -> 50%).

Anya K: logging the follow-ups in the canary PR and eval dashboard. will tag folks when first 1k canary requests complete.

Sam H: one final ask — add a short A/B prompt set for user-facing QA so product can review a sample of live outputs before we widen traffic.

Anya K: will do.

(ends)
